description: Welcome to Space Pulses! We are a passionate, multidisciplinary team of university students combining technical engineering, software development, and biological sciences to tackle real-world challenges in the NASA Space Apps Challenge.
summary:
ASTRA-MED
Every Heartbeat Has a Mission.

We celebrate every human step toward the stars. Yet behind every astronaut reaching for the unknown is a human body silently enduring the extraordinary.

Far from Earth, astronauts are separated from loved ones and immediate medical care. In microgravity, muscles weaken, bones lose density, vision shifts, and normal bodily functions are strained. Prolonged isolation impacts psychological well-being and cognitive performance, while oral health issues, medication risks, and infections become harder to manage in a confined spacecraft. Millions of miles from help, even a minor health concern can become critical.

ِASTRA-MED addresses these interconnected challenges through one integrated, AI-assisted astronaut healthcare platform. It combines continuous vital signs monitoring, muscle and bone assessment, vision and oral health screening, cognitive testing, immersive psychological support, medication management, and infection surveillance. An interactive 3D astronaut model visualizes findings, uniting health data for early awareness and timely intervention.

Our vision goes beyond monitoring numbers. We aim to protect the person behind the spacesuit—because the greatest achievement of space exploration is not simply reaching another world, but bringing every astronaut safely home.

1. OUR VISION & THE PROBLEM WE SOLVE

As NASA prepares to send astronauts back to the Moon under the Artemis program and eventually to Mars, crews will travel millions of miles away from Earth. At that distance, radio messages take up to 22 minutes to reach Earth and another 22 minutes to come back. This means live video calls with doctors and emergency rescue missions are impossible.

ASTRA-MED solves this problem. It is a smart, 100% offline medical system and AI health assistant that lives right inside the spacecraft. It helps astronauts check their own health, spot early warning signs, and treat medical issues without needing an internet connection or help from Earth.

2. HOW IT WORKS: 24/7 TRACKING & ULTRA-LOW POWER (0.4W)

On a spaceship, electricity is precious, and keeping surfaces germ-free is critical. Running a bright computer screen all day wastes too much energy. To save power, ASTRA-MED stays in a quiet "sleep mode" that uses only 0.4 Watts of electricity—less than a tiny nightlight.

Meanwhile, a comfortable smartwatch worn by the astronaut checks 7 key health signs every single second:

  • Heart Rate: Checks how fast and steady the heart is beating.
  • Blood Pressure: Tracks how blood flows when there is no gravity.
  • Blood Oxygen: Makes sure the astronaut is getting enough oxygen from recycled cabin air.
  • Blood Sugar: Prevents sudden energy crashes during demanding spacewalks.
  • Body Temperature: Catches early signs of a fever or hidden infection.
  • Sleep Quality: Measures how many hours the astronaut sleeps and how restful it is.
  • Mood & Stress Level: Tracks mental fatigue, loneliness, and daily stress.

Two Smart Ways the System Wakes Up:

  • Automatic Emergency Wake-Up: The exact second any of the 7 health signs goes outside a safe range, the screen wakes up automatically, sounds a gentle alert, and tells the astronaut what to do.
  • Touchless Hand-Gesture Wake-Up: When an astronaut wants to check their health manually, they do not even need to touch the screen. Using a small camera and computer vision (Python, OpenCV, and MediaPipe), the astronaut simply opens their hand and closes it into a fist in the air. This keeps screens germ-free and works easily even when wearing thick spacesuit gloves.

3. PROTECTING ASTRONAUTS FROM NASA’S 5 SPACE HAZARDS

Space is a harsh place. ASTRA-MED protects astronauts from all 5 major dangers identified by NASA (Space Radiation, Isolation, Distance from Earth, Lack of Gravity, and Closed Spacecraft Environments):

A. Brain Health & Eye Pressure
  • The Risk: Without Earth's gravity pulling fluids down, body fluids float up toward the head. This puts pressure on the brain and flattens the back of the eyeballs, causing blurry vision (known as SANS).
  • How ASTRA-MED Helps: Reminds astronauts to do a quick, painless eye-pressure check every 7 days and turns on special blue-tinted cabin lights to help balance their body clock and fluid levels.
B. Mental Health & Stress Support
  • The Risk: Living in a small, cramped spaceship for months or years away from family causes stress, poor sleep, and burnout.
  • How ASTRA-MED Helps: Acts as an offline AI wellness companion. It notices when stress rises or sleep drops, checks in daily with the astronaut, and guides them through calming breathing and mental relaxation exercises.
C. Space Dental Care (Preventing Severe Tooth Pain)
  • The Risk: A bad toothache can ruin a space mission. When astronauts put on spacesuits for a spacewalk, air pressure drops quickly. Tiny air bubbles trapped under old dental fillings can expand and cause extreme tooth pain. Stress also causes astronauts to grind their teeth at night.
  • How ASTRA-MED Helps: Guides astronauts through a simple Monthly Dental Checkup:
  1. Uses a tiny mouth camera to check fillings and crowns for small cracks before a spacewalk.
  2. Checks gums for early bleeding or swelling.
  3. Tests teeth for sensitivity to hot, cold, or pressure.
  4. Checks for jaw clenching and reminds the astronaut to wear a protective night guard.
D. Fighting Hidden Germs & Weakened Immunity
  • The Risk: Space travel weakens the human immune system, while bacteria inside closed cabins can grow stronger and old viruses (like chickenpox or shingles) can wake back up.
  • How ASTRA-MED Helps: Spots tiny rises in body temperature and heart rate before the astronaut even feels sick, recommending early hygiene steps, isolation, and targeted treatments.
E. Safe Space Medicines & Expiration Tracking
  • The Risk: Space radiation breaks down medicines faster than on Earth, and zero gravity changes how the human body absorbs pills. Standard Earth doses might not work—or could be too strong.
  • How ASTRA-MED Helps: The offline AI Doctor calculates the exact safe dose for zero gravity based on the astronaut's current vitals and tracks radiation levels to warn the crew if any medicine in the kit has lost its strength.
F. Keeping Bones & Hearts Strong
  • The Risk: Without gravity, astronauts lose 1% to 1.5% of their bone strength every month, and their heart muscles get weaker.
  • How ASTRA-MED Helps: Adjusts daily fitness goals based on where the astronaut is (floating in space, on the Moon, or on Mars), guiding their 2-hour daily workouts, water intake, and Vitamin D supplements.

4. EASY TO USE FOR EVERY ASTRONAUT

  • Clickable 3D Body Scanner: Astronauts see a 3D model of the human body with simple color codes: Cyan (Healthy), Amber (Needs Attention), and Red (Urgent Action). Clicking any body part explains how it works in plain language, why a test is needed, and step-by-step instructions—assuming zero medical training.
  • Easy-to-Read Health Charts: Interactive graphs show how health numbers change over weeks and months so slow problems are caught early.
  • Works Anywhere in Space: Automatically updates health rules whether the crew is inside a spaceship (0g), on the Moon (1/6th gravity), or on Mars (1/3rd gravity).
  • Fun Motivation & Rewards (Gamification): Tracks a daily "Mission Readiness Score" and rewards streaks for completing workouts, mental check-ins, and monthly dental scans.
  • Clear Step-by-Step Help: Minor issues give self-care tips; medium issues alert the crew's onboard medic; major emergencies pack the data into a small file to send back to NASA doctors on Earth.

5. REAL-LIFE EXAMPLE: STOPPING A SPACEWALK EMERGENCY

To show how ASTRA-MED works in action, we simulated a real mission scenario on the way to Mars:

  • The Warning Sign: 6 hours before a spacewalk, the smartwatch notices the astronaut's resting heart rate jumped from 64 to 88 beats per minute, stress is high, and cabin carbon dioxide (CO2) is slightly elevated.
  • Automatic Check: ASTRA-MED wakes up from its 0.4W sleep mode, highlights the head/jaw and chest areas in Amber on the 3D body map, and asks the astronaut to do a quick mouth-camera scan.
  • The Save: The offline AI finds a tiny crack under a back tooth filling. Going on a spacewalk with that crack would have caused severe tooth pain inside the helmet. ASTRA-MED advises delaying the spacewalk by 12 hours, applying a quick temporary dental seal from the medical kit, and refreshing the cabin air—preventing a dangerous emergency.

6. TOOLS & TECHNOLOGY WE USED

  • Website & 3D Body Model: HTML5, CSS3, JavaScript, Interactive 3D Human Model, and Health Trend Charts.
  • Touchless Camera & AI Brain: Python, OpenCV, Google MediaPipe (tracks 21 hand points for gesture control), and Offline AI Medical Logic.
  • Smartwatch Hardware Prototype: ESP32 microcontroller, mini OLED display screen, and biometric sensors running on a 0.4W low-power design.
  • Design & Video: Canva, Prezi, and custom dark-mode space interface design.

7. HELPING PEOPLE BACK ON EARTH

The same technology built for Mars can save lives right here on Earth:

  • Germ-Free Hospital Operating Rooms: Surgeons can use our touchless hand gestures to check patient scans and heart rates during surgery without ever touching a dirty screen.
  • Remote Villages & Disaster Zones: Doctors in areas without internet or reliable electricity can run our 0.4W offline AI medical assistant on basic devices.
  • Next Steps: Adding portable ultrasound image reading and needle-free blood sugar tracking in future versions.

8. OUR TEAM: SPACE PULSES

  • Mohammad Ateir (Team Leader — Electronics & Robotics Engineering): Built the system architecture, website, 3D interactive body model, smartwatch hardware prototype, and touchless hand-gesture camera system.
  • Mohammad Alzoubi (Dentistry): Created the visual design, user interface, branding, and mission story.
  • Kinda AbuBaker (Dentistry): Researched NASA astronaut health data and designed the medical, mental wellness, and preventive dental checkup guides.
